metadata.title: Soil Organic Carbon: the hidden potential
metadata.publisher: Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO)

summary: FAO synthesis on the foundational role of soil organic carbon in biological diversity, soil physical stability, and hydrological resilience.

sections.text: Soil organic carbon (SOC) is critical for structural stability, moisture holding capacity, and microbial biodiversity. In low-rainfall regions, each 1% increase in SOC can enhance available soil water capacity by up to 15-20 mm per meter of soil depth, markedly improving crop survival during seasonal dry spells.

Depletion of SOC below 1.0% triggers a severe reduction in soil biological diversity, limiting enzymatic nutrient cycling. Rebuilding carbon inputs fosters diverse bacterial and fungal consortia essential for root symbiosis.
